# GenieX CLI Reference

Complete reference for the `geniex` CLI (Qualcomm GenieX), the engine behind LocalGenie.
Generated by scanning `geniex --help` and every subcommand's `--help`.

## Global flags (apply to all commands)

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--data-dir <string>` | Custom data directory (env: `GENIEX_DATADIR`) |
| `--log <string>` | Log level: `none`, `error`, `warn`, `info`, `debug`, `trace` (env: `GENIEX_LOG`, default `none`) |
| `--skip-update` | Skip checking for updates |
| `--verbose` | Enable verbose output |
| `-h, --help` | Help for the command |
| `-v, --version` | Print version information (top level only) |

## Command groups

- **Model commands:** `pull`, `remove`, `clean`, `list`, `model`
- **Inference commands:** `infer`, `serve`, `run`
- **Management commands:** `config`, `version`, `update`
- **Other:** `help`, `completion`

---

## Model commands

### `geniex pull <model-name>[:<precision>]`
Download and cache a model by name. Append `:<precision>` to pick a precision; otherwise you are prompted. Docker Hub models (e.g. `docker.io/ai/gemma3` or `ai/gemma3` with `--model-hub docker`) use `:<tag>` instead — omit it for `latest`.

Flags:
- `--model-hub <string>` — hub to use: `aihub` | `hf` | `modelscope` | `docker` | `localfs`. **Auto-detected when omitted.**
- `--local-path <string>` — path to a local directory or AI Hub `.zip` file. Implies `--model-hub localfs`.
- `--model-type <string>` — model type: `llm` | `vlm`. **Auto-detected when omitted.**

Notes:
- `pull` copies files into the GenieX cache; after a successful pull the source can be safely deleted.
- For GGUF models the CLI prompts for a precision (e.g. `Q4_0` [1.2 GiB] default, `Q8_0`, `F16`). `Q4_0` has the best Hexagon NPU support.
- Qualcomm AI Hub models are pre-quantized — no precision choice needed.
- Passing `--model-type llm` at pull time writes the same manifest field as `model set-type`, so a fresh pull needs no `set-type` afterwards.

### `geniex remove <model-name>[:<precision>]...` (alias: `rm`)
Delete one or more cached models. With `:<precision>`, removes only that precision; otherwise the whole model.

Flags:
- `-y, --yes` — skip the confirmation prompt

### `geniex clean`
Remove **all** cached models and free up storage.

Flags:
- `-y, --yes` — skip the confirmation prompt

### `geniex list` (alias: `ls`)
Display all cached models. `--format json|csv` gives machine-readable output with a stable schema; `--verbose` only affects the table view.

Flags:
- `--format <string>` — `table` | `json` | `csv` (default `table`)

### `geniex model`
Manage cached models.

#### `geniex model set-type <model-name> [llm|vlm]`
Override the model type stored in a cached model's manifest. Omit the type argument to choose interactively.

The type decides which path `geniex infer` takes: `vlm` loads the mmproj projector alongside the weights and accepts image/audio input; `llm` loads language weights only. Forcing a multimodal GGUF to `llm` is how you run its text path when weights + projector don't fit in memory.

#### `geniex model list`
List Qualcomm AI Hub models geniex can run (those with a qairt/NPU build). By default only models compatible with the current device are shown. Names are ready to pull, e.g. `geniex pull qualcomm/Qwen3-4B`.

Flags:
- `--all` — list every model, not just device-compatible ones

## Inference commands

### `geniex infer <model-name>[:<precision>]`
Run inference locally with a cached model. Prompts for precision if omitted.

### `geniex run <model-name>[:<precision>]`
Infer via the GenieX server (server must be running; model must be cached). Same flags as `infer`.

### Shared LLM/VLM flags (`infer` and `run`)

Sampler flags:
| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--temperature <float32>` | Sampling temperature |
| `--top-p <float32>` | Top-p sampling |
| `--top-k <int32>` | Top-k sampling |
| `--min-p <float32>` | Min-p sampling |
| `--repetition-penalty <float32>` | Repetition penalty (default 1) |
| `--presence-penalty <float32>` | Presence penalty |
| `--frequency-penalty <float32>` | Frequency penalty |
| `--seed <int32>` | Random seed |
| `--grammar-path <string>` | Path to a GBNF grammar file for constrained generation |
| `--grammar-string <string>` | Inline grammar in GBNF string format |
| `--enable-json` | Force JSON-only output (documented in official docs; not shown in current CLI `--help`) |

Model flags:
| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `-c, --compute <string>` | Compute unit: `cpu`, `gpu`, `npu`, `hybrid`, or explicit device list like `HTP0,HTP1,HTP2,HTP3` (llama_cpp only; default `npu`) |
| `-n, --ngl <int32>` | Layers offloaded to gpu/npu, `-1` = all (llama_cpp only; default -1) |
| `--nctx <int32>` | Context window size (llama_cpp only; default 4096) |
| `--max-tokens <int32>` | Max tokens (default 2048) |
| `--stop <stringArray>` | Stop sequences (llama_cpp only) |
| `--stop-file <string>` | File containing stop sequences (llama_cpp only) |
| `--think` | Thinking mode; `--think=false` to disable (default true) |
| `-s, --system-prompt <string>` | System prompt |
| `-i, --input <string>` | Prompt from a txt file |
| `-p, --prompt <stringArray>` | Pass prompt (also the VLM prompt flag) |
| `-t, --token-file <string>` | Token file with space-separated token IDs (llama_cpp only) |
| `--sliding-window` | Evict oldest context on overflow instead of erroring (qairt only) |
| `--power-mode <string>` | HTP power/clock-management mode, shared by `qairt` and `llama_cpp`: `low_power_saver`, `power_saver`, `high_power_saver`, `low_balanced`, `balanced`, `high_performance`, `sustained_high_performance`, `burst` (default `burst`; documented in official docs, not shown in current CLI `--help`) |
| `--spec-type <string>` | Speculative decoding types, comma-separated: `draft-mtp`, `draft-eagle3`, `draft-simple`, `ngram-simple`, `ngram-map-k`, `ngram-map-k4v`, `ngram-mod`, `ngram-cache` (llama_cpp only) |
| `--draft-model <string>` | Draft/MTP model for `draft-*` spec types: catalogue name or local GGUF path (llama_cpp only) |
| `--draft-tokens <int32>` | Max draft tokens per step (llama_cpp only; default 3) |
| `--draft-min <int32>` | Min draft tokens per step, 0 = llama.cpp default (llama_cpp only) |
| `--draft-p-min <float32>` | Min greedy draft probability, 0 = llama.cpp default (llama_cpp only) |

### Speculative decoding / MTP (llama_cpp only, text-only)

MTP (Multi-Token Prediction) uses a draft model trained **alongside the exact target** — an arbitrary small GGUF cannot be substituted; a mismatched pair fails at load time. Both models are resident at once, so plan for ~20 GB disk and enough RAM for the pair.

| Flag | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `--spec-type` | off | Set to `draft-mtp` to enable MTP |
| `--draft-model` | — | Catalogue name `org/repo[:precision]` or local GGUF path. Required by `draft-mtp` |
| `--draft-tokens` | 3 | Max draft tokens per verification step |
| `--draft-min` | 0 | Min draft tokens per step; 0 = llama.cpp default |
| `--draft-p-min` | 0 | Draft stops proposing below this confidence; 0 = llama.cpp default |

Example:

```sh
geniex infer google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-qat-q4_0-gguf:Q4_0 \
  --spec-type draft-mtp \
  --draft-model RachidAR/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-qat-assistant-q4_0-gguf:Q4_0 \
  --draft-tokens 3
```

- When active, the profiling block gains a `draft accept` line (e.g. `draft accept: 14/75 (18.7%)`) — accepted draft tokens over total proposed. That line confirms it engaged.
- Setup failure is non-fatal: if the draft context can't be built, geniex logs `speculative decoding setup failed; falling back to plain decoding` and continues at normal speed.
- On the `qairt` runtime these settings are ignored with a warning. Enabling it on a multimodal model runs the LLM path and drops image/audio content with a warning.

### Server-side MTP (`POST /v1/chat/completions`)

Speculation is configured **per request** — `geniex serve` has no `--spec-type` flag. The request body takes the same settings as `spec_*` fields:

- `spec_type` — e.g. `"draft-mtp"`
- `spec_draft_model` — the draft model name
- `spec_n_max` — same as `--draft-tokens`
- `spec_n_min` / `spec_p_min` — same as `--draft-min` / `--draft-p-min`

Notes:
- **The server never auto-downloads a draft model** — it only uses what's already cached; a missing draft errors mid-request. Pull the draft first.
- The `spec_*` fields are part of the model cache key, so changing any of them rebuilds the model on the next request. Keep them stable across a run.
- Try it in the built-in Swagger UI at `http://127.0.0.1:18181`.

Multi-HTP note: with an explicit device list like `HTP0,HTP1,HTP2,HTP3`, set `GGML_HEXAGON_NDEV=4` to match the number of device IDs (llama.cpp + multi-DSP devices only). The device list bypasses the `npu`/`hybrid` aliases — `npu` pins `HTP0` alone, while a comma-separated list distributes across all named cores. `qairt` models coerce a device list to NPU with a warning.

### VLM specifics (`infer`)
- Image (`.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.png`, `.webp`) and audio (`.wav`, `.mp3`) paths in the prompt are auto-detected; use absolute paths. A single prompt can carry both image and audio.
- Audio input runs on the **llama.cpp** backend only and needs an audio-capable model (mmproj with a conformer encoder). QAIRT models report `audio: false` and fail with `GenieXError(-201201): Multimodal generation failed` when given audio.
- In an interactive session with an audio-capable model, `/mic` records a clip (Ctrl-C stops and transcribes). Requires **SoX** on `PATH` (`winget install --id=ChrisBagwell.SoX -e` on Windows); without it geniex warns `SoX is not installed`.

### Context length constraints
- **llama.cpp (GGUF):** `--nctx <N>` raises the window at runtime up to the model's trained maximum; larger windows use more KV-cache memory.
- **qairt (NPU):** context length is **baked into the compiled bundle** — `--nctx` has no effect. Use `--sliding-window` to keep chatting past the limit, or pull a bundle compiled for a longer context from Qualcomm AI Hub.

### `geniex serve`
Run the GenieX server — an **OpenAI-compatible** local server (see the official "Local server" docs for the API).

| Flag | Env | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--host <string>` | `GENIEX_HOST` | Server address (default `127.0.0.1:18181`) |
| `--origins <string>` | `GENIEX_ORIGINS` | CORS origins (default `*`) |
| `--keepalive <int>` | `GENIEX_KEEPALIVE` | Keepalive seconds (default 300) |
| `--nctx <int32>` | `GENIEX_NCTX` | Default context window, llama_cpp only (default 4096) |
| `-n, --ngl <int32>` | `GENIEX_NGL` | Default offloaded layers, llama_cpp only (default -1) |
| `-c, --compute <string>` | `GENIEX_COMPUTE` | Default compute unit: `cpu`, `gpu`, `npu`, `hybrid` |
| `--https` | `GENIEX_HTTPS` | Enable HTTPS/TLS |
| `--certfile <string>` | `GENIEX_CERTFILE` | TLS certificate file (default `cert.pem`) |
| `--keyfile <string>` | `GENIEX_KEYFILE` | TLS private key file (default `key.pem`) |

Server API note: to move a thinking model's chain-of-thought out of `message.content` into `message.reasoning_content`, set the per-request `reasoning_format` field.

## Management commands

### `geniex config`
Manage CLI configuration. Available key: `chipset`.

- `geniex config get <key>` — retrieve a value
- `geniex config set <key> [value]` — set a value (empty string clears it; for `chipset`, omit the value for an interactive picker)
- `geniex config list` — list all keys and values (unset keys shown blank)

### `geniex version`
Show the geniex version.

### `geniex update`
Update geniex to the latest version.

Flags:
- `--silent` — run the installer silently (no prompts or progress UI)

---

## Other

### `geniex help [command]`
Help for any command.

### `geniex completion [bash|zsh|fish|powershell]`
Generate shell autocompletion scripts.

## `geniex-bench` (standalone binary)

`geniex-bench` is a separate benchmark binary (not part of the `geniex` CLI) that measures TTFT, prefill speed, and decode speed directly against the GenieX C API. It has no CLI dependency — download the archive, extract, and run. Ships pre-built for Windows ARM64 and Linux ARM64.

### Install

- **Windows ARM64:** download `https://qaihub-public-assets.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/qai-hub-geniex/geniex-bench-windows-arm64.zip`, extract, run `.\bench\bin\geniex-bench.exe --help`.
- **Linux ARM64:** download `https://qaihub-public-assets.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/qai-hub-geniex/geniex-bench-linux-arm64.tar.gz`, extract, then set `LD_LIBRARY_PATH="$BENCH_DIR/lib:$BENCH_DIR/lib/llama_cpp"` and `GENIEX_PLUGIN_PATH="$BENCH_DIR/lib"` for the session.
- **Pin a version:** append `-v0.3.19` (or any version) to the filename in the URL.
- **Prerequisites:** Snapdragon X Elite/X2 Elite (Windows) or Dragonwing IQ-9075/IQ-8275 (Linux, needs `qcom-adreno1`, `qcom-fastrpc1`, `libqnn1`). A pulled model, or a HF/AI Hub model id that geniex-bench downloads automatically on first use (via `--mm-data-dir`).

### Usage

Minimum required flags: `--plugin`, `--device`, `-m`. The model accepts a local path or a model-manager id (auto-downloaded on first use):

```sh
geniex-bench --plugin llama_cpp --device npu -m bartowski/Qwen_Qwen3-0.6B-GGUF:Q4_0
# [ok] cell plugin=llama_cpp device=npu ngl=999 ttft=349.2ms prefill=60.2tps decode=21.8tps gen=128 tok
```

Defaults: 1 warmup + 5 measured repetitions, 512 random input tokens, 128 generated tokens, temperature 0.0 (deterministic), seed 42. Numbers are aggregated as median ± stdev.

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--plugin` | — | `llama_cpp` \| `qairt`. **Required.** |
| `--device` | `auto` | `cpu` \| `gpu` \| `npu` \| `hybrid` |
| `-m, --model` | — | Local path (`.gguf` or bundle dir) or model-manager id (`org/repo[:quant]`). **Required.** |
| `-c, --ctx-size` | 512 | Random-token prefill length |
| `-n, --n-gen` | 128 | Tokens to generate per run |
| `-r` | 5 | Measured repetitions |
| `--warmup` | 1 | Warmup runs (not counted in stats) |
| `--temperature` | 0.0 | Sampling temperature; `0.0` = deterministic (greedy) |
| `--seed` | 42 | Random seed for prefill token generation |
| `--power-mode` | `burst` | HTP power/clock-management mode (same values as `infer`) |
| `--output-json` | — | Write per-cell JSON with aggregated stats to this path |
| `--cell-id` | — | Label for the JSON report |
| `--matrix-file` | — | TSV file (`cell_id`, `plugin`, `device`, `model`) to run multiple cells in one session |
| `--output-json-dir` | — | Output directory for matrix-mode JSON files (one JSON per row) |
| `--mm-data-dir` | — | Model-manager data dir; lets geniex-bench download models on first use |
| `--accuracy` | — | Print generated text instead of timing (1 run, no warmup); pair with `--prompt-file` |

### Reading the numbers

- **ttft** — time to first token (includes the media encoder on VLM runs, so not comparable to text-only TTFT).
- **prefill (tok/s)** — input processing speed. For `--plugin qairt`, reported over the padded length (`ceil(n/128) × 128`) because QAIRT pads input to 128-token chunks.
- **decode (tok/s)** — generation speed; the number users perceive.

### Device guidance

| Device | Best for |
|---|---|
| `hybrid` | Fastest on llama_cpp models — per-tensor scheduler routes each op to HTP or CPU. Default recommendation. |
| `npu` | Pins to a single HTP session; deterministic compute-unit layout. Slower prefill than hybrid on most models. |
| `cpu` | Baseline; uses `ngl=0`. |
| `gpu` | OpenCL path; for GPU vs NPU comparisons on llama_cpp models. |

`--plugin qairt` runs on NPU only — `--device cpu/gpu/hybrid` are silently coerced to `npu`.

### Fair comparisons

Hold constant: context size (`-c`), generated tokens (`-n`), temperature, seed, repetitions. Common mistakes:
- Comparing Q4_0 vs Q8_0 (larger file = slower decode regardless of backend).
- Comparing `--device cpu` (`ngl=0`) against `--device npu` (`ngl=-1`, all layers offloaded).
- First run after a model pull includes download time in wallclock but **not** in the reported ttft/prefill/decode numbers (measured inside the engine), so numbers stay valid.

### JSON output

`--output-json` writes per-run timing plus aggregated stats (median/min/max/mean/stdev) with `schema_version: "2"`, keyed by `cell_id`, `plugin`, `device`, and an `agg` object with `ttft_ms`, `prefill_tps`, `decode_tps`.

### Matrix mode

`--matrix-file` is a TSV with columns `cell_id`, `plugin`, `device`, `model_path_or_id`; each row produces one JSON file in `--output-json-dir`, amortising plugin init cost across cells.

## LocalGenie integration notes

- LocalGenie talks to `geniex serve` on port `18181` (persisted in the `user_preferences` table).
- Model lifecycle (pull/list/remove) maps to `src-tauri/src/commands/models.rs`; server lifecycle to `server.rs`; chat/inference to `chat.rs`.
- When changing model/server flows, always validate the known blocker: model loading and chat completion hang when the server does not respond to the warmup request.
